description.value: This study investigated functional brain responses to personalized neutral/relaxing, stressful, and favorite-food cues in adolescents with prenatal cocaine exposure and non-cocaine exposure.

spans.text: Twenty-two adolescents with PCE and 22 age-, gender-, and IQ-matched non-cocaine exposed (NCE) adolescents underwent functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) during exposure to individually personalized neutral/relaxing, stressful, and favorite-food cues.

description.value: Observational, cross-sectional comparison of adolescents with prenatal cocaine exposure and non-cocaine exposure.

spans.text: Anatomical images of the functional slice locations were acquired using a spin-echo sequence in the axial plane parallel to the anterior–posterior commissure line (repetition time/echo time (TR/TE)=300/2.46 ms, bandwidth=310 Hz/pixel, flip angle=60°, field of view (FOV)=220 mm × 220 mm, matrix=256 × 256, slice thickness=4 mm (no skip), 32 slices).

name.value: personalized neutral/relaxing, stressful, and favorite-food cues

spans.text: Twenty-two adolescents with PCE and 22 age-, gender-, and IQ-matched non-cocaine exposed (NCE) adolescents underwent functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) during exposure to individually personalized neutral/relaxing, stressful, and favorite-food cues.

description.value: Participants heard individually tailored audiotaped scripts designed to induce neutral-relaxing, stressful, or appetitive states during fMRI scanning.

spans.text: In this fMRI task, audiotaped personalized scripts based on individual interviews are presented de novo to the participant during scanning in order to induce either stress, craving or neutral–relaxed states (block design).
Appetitive
Appetitive scripts

description.value: Participants listened to an individualized script describing a recent experience in which they wanted and then consumed their favorite food, and were asked to engage in appetitive imagery and craving. Scripts were calibrated to events rated at least 8 out of 10 for pleasure.

spans.text: Appetitive scripts were based on participants' descriptions of recent times when they wanted and then consumed their favorite food (eg, pizza, ice cream)
Stress
Stress scripts

description.value: Participants listened to an individualized script describing a personally stressful life event during which they felt sad, mad, or upset and could not change the situation, and were asked to engage in stressful imagery. Scripts were calibrated to events rated at least 8 out of 10 for stress.

spans.text: Stress scripts were based on participants' descriptions of life events during which they felt ‘sad, mad or upset in that moment and could not do anything to change the situation'
Neutral–relaxing
Neutral–relaxing scripts

description.value: Participants listened to an individualized script describing a commonly experienced neutral or relaxing situation, such as sitting in a park or relaxing in their room, and were asked to engage in neutral-relaxing imagery.

spans.text: block design
Participants responded verbally

instructions.value: Participants underwent relaxation and guided-imagery training before scanning, then listened to personalized scripts while imagining neutral-relaxing, stressful, or favorite-food experiences.

spans.text: all participants conducted a relaxation and guided-imagery training session before scanning

stimuli.value: Six individually tailored audiotaped scripts presented through headphones: two neutral-relaxing, two stressful, and two favorite-food scripts, each approximately 2.5 minutes long.

spans.text: each participant was exposed to six individually tailored audiotaped scripts (two neutral–relaxing, two stressful and two appetitive)
